text:
Lightsail
pip install 'vpseasy[aws]' and set AWS_PROFILE (any standard AWS credential source works). Lightsail has the same methods as Hetzner, so vps_deploy() takes either. create() is idempotent, attaches a static IP, opens only port 22 (traffic arrives through the Cloudflare tunnel) and turns on daily snapshots. Region defaults to Sydney (ap-southeast-2).

ls = Lightsail()
r = vps_deploy('lh', _app, ls, bundle='small_3_2')
print(f'Deployed at {r.ip}, key: {r.key}')

Lightsail runs user data as a shell script rather than cloud-config, so create() converts vps_init() YAML with cloud_init_sh(). The script keeps the YAML verbatim, applies the same settings, and touches /var/lib/vpseasy/ready for wait_ready():

ud = cloud_init_sh(vps_init('demo', ['ssh-ed25519 AAAA... demo']).yaml)
print(ud[ud.index('hostnamectl'):][:600])

title: vpseasy
text:
Docker Compose helpers
Any app that dockeasy can build — FastHTML, FastAPI, Go, Rust, Node — follows the same production Compose shape when deployed behind Cloudflare Tunnel: an app service, a caddy reverse proxy, a cloudflared tunnel container, a shared web network, and two named volumes for Caddy state.
caddy_stack() generates that structure from a domain and any dockeasy Dockerfile object. vols_to_binds() converts absolute container paths to local bind mounts. The root= argument saves all three files (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, Caddyfile); without it the Compose object is returned without writing anything.

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
df = fasthtml_app(pkgs=['sqlite3'], vols=['/app/data'], healthcheck='/health')
c = caddy_stack('myapp.example.com', df, vols=['/app/data'], root=d)
print(c)

services:
  app:
    build: .
    volumes:
    - ./data:/app/data
    env_file:
    - .env
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
    - web
  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    depends_on:
    - app
    volumes:
    - /private/var/folders/kg/9vdw4mdd1fs58svgh4k1qhr09x7dqh/T/tmpfs6cqxh2/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile
    - caddy_data:/data
    - caddy_config:/config
    networks:
    - web
    restart: unless-stopped
  cloudflared:
    image: cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
    command: tunnel --no-autoupdate run --url http://caddy
    environment:
    - TUNNEL_TOKEN=${CF_TUNNEL_TOKEN}
    networks:
    - web
    restart: unless-stopped
networks:
  web: null
volumes:
  caddy_data: null
  caddy_config: null

title: vpseasy
text:
Litestream backups
Litestream streams each SQLite db to an S3-compatible bucket: a Lightsail bucket, AWS S3 or Cloudflare R2 (endpoint='https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com', region='auto'). Lightsail.bucket() creates the bucket and an access key; put them in .env as LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID / LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY. Lightsail allows two keys per bucket and shows each secret once.

b = Lightsail().bucket('lh-backups')
b.bucket, b.endpoint, b.key_id

litestream_conf() writes litestream.yml. Db paths are container paths inside the app’s volumes; each replica lives under <prefix>/<db path>:

d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
print(litestream_conf(['/app/data/app.db'], 'lh-backups', endpoint='https://s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com',
                      region='ap-southeast-2', prefix='lh', conf=d/'litestream.yml'))

snapshot:
  interval: 24h
  retention: 72h
validation:
  interval: 12h
dbs:
- path: /app/data/app.db
  replica:
    type: s3
    bucket: lh-backups
    path: lh/app/data/app.db
    region: ap-southeast-2
    access-key-id: ${LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
    secret-access-key: ${LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
    endpoint: https://s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com



caddy_stack(..., litestream=...) adds two services. A one-shot litestream-restore must finish before app starts, so a fresh server gets its db back before the app can create an empty one; the litestream replicate service starts after app:

c = caddy_stack('lh.example.com', fasthtml_app(vols=['/app/data']), vols=['/app/data'], root=d,
                litestream=dict(dbs=['/app/data/app.db'], bucket='lh-backups', region='ap-southeast-2', prefix='lh',
                                endpoint='https://s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com'))
svcs = c.to_dict()['services']
print(yaml.safe_dump({k: {o: v[o] for o in ('image', 'command', 'depends_on', 'restart') if o in v} for k,v in svcs.items()
                      if k in ('app', 'litestream-restore', 'litestream')}, sort_keys=False))

app:
  depends_on:
    litestream-restore:
      condition: service_completed_successfully
  restart: unless-stopped
litestream-restore:
  image: litestream/litestream:0.5
  command: restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists /app/data/app.db
  restart: 'no'
litestream:
  image: litestream/litestream:0.5
  command: replicate
  depends_on:
  - app
  restart: unless-stopped

text:
Lightsail (boto3)
Lightsail has the same shape as Hetzner (servers, get, server_ip, create, delete) over the boto3 Lightsail client, so vps_deploy works with either. boto3 is an optional extra: pip install 'vpseasy[aws]'. Credentials come from the standard AWS chain (e.g. AWS_PROFILE from SSO). create() is idempotent, attaches a static IP, opens only port 22 (traffic arrives through the Cloudflare tunnel) and enables daily automatic snapshots.
Lightsail runs user data as a shell launch script, not as cloud-config, so create() converts vps_init() YAML with cloud_init_sh(): a POSIX script that applies the same settings (hostname, users with sudo and SSH keys, write_files, apt conf, packages, runcmd), keeps the YAML in /var/lib/vpseasy/cloud-config.yaml, logs to /var/log/vpseasy-init.log and touches /var/lib/vpseasy/ready (or error), which chk_cloud_init() reads. Re-running cloud-init with the YAML in /etc/cloud/cloud.cfg.d was tried on Ubuntu 24.04 and did not create users, so it is not used.


source

cloud_init_sh
def cloud_init_sh(
    cloud_init
):
POSIX shell equivalent of a vps_init() cloud-config, for providers that run user data as a script (Lightsail). Skips power_state (no reboot), preserve_hostname and disable_root (root login is already off on Ubuntu images).

@contextmanager
def patch_to_fakes(calls):
    'Replace wait_ready, deploy, vps_init and subprocess with fakes where vps_deploy resolves them, so no key or known_hosts is touched.'
    g = vps_deploy.__globals__
    ks = 'wait_ready', 'deploy', 'vps_init', 'subprocess'
    o = {k: g[k] for k in ks}
    g['wait_ready'] = lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('wait_ready', a, k))
    g['deploy'] = lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('deploy', a, k))
    g['vps_init'] = lambda name, *a, **k: AttrDict(yaml='#cloud-config\n', key='/tmp/k')
    g['subprocess'] = AttrDict(run=lambda *a, **k: calls.append(('ssh-keygen', a, k)))
    try: yield
    finally: g.update(o)

    def create(self, name, cloud_init=None, **kw): self.made.append(name); self.kw = kw; return AttrDict(ip='192.0.2.9', name=name, key='/tmp/k')

text:
Litestream
litestream_conf() writes a Litestream 0.5 config that streams each SQLite db to an S3-compatible bucket (a Lightsail.bucket(), AWS S3 or Cloudflare R2) under <prefix>/<db path>, so dbs with the same file name never collide. Tested against litestream/litestream:0.5 (v0.5.17); note Litestream ignores unknown config keys silently. litestream_svc() returns a Litestream service’s Compose.svc() kwargs. caddy_stack(..., litestream=dict(dbs=..., bucket=..., endpoint=..., region=...)) wires them in: a one-shot litestream-restore service (restore -if-db-not-exists -if-replica-exists) must complete successfully before app starts, so a fresh server gets its db back before the app can create an empty one; the long-running litestream replicate service starts after app. Credentials come from LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID / LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in .env. Db paths are container paths and must sit inside one of the app’s vols, otherwise the sidecar would replicate nothing.

Always use the private key path (no .pub) with -i. The public key is for authorized_keys, not for SSH client auth.

Lightsail runs user data as a shell script, so Lightsail.create() converts vps_init() cloud-config with cloud_init_sh() (supports hostname, users, write_files, apt conf, packages, runcmd; other keys raise). Progress: /var/log/vpseasy-init.log, done marker /var/lib/vpseasy/ready.
Lightsail bundle ids change over time (small_3_0 is gone; current ones end in _3_2). List them with Lightsail()._c.get_bundles().
Litestream db paths must be absolute container paths inside one of the app’s vols; litestream_conf raises ValueError otherwise. A one-shot litestream-restore service must complete before app starts (condition: service_completed_successfully); the litestream replicate service starts after app. Verified end to end with litestream/litestream:0.5 (v0.5.17): empty bucket → restore exits 0; wiped server → db restored before app.
Always use the private key path (no .pub) with -i. The public key is for authorized_keys, not for SSH client auth.
